evidence.summary: Pre-check before password verify, constant-shape dummy PBKDF2 hash for unknown users (closes both status/body and timing enumeration channels), HMAC log keys, in-memory-only state (no cip write), bounded key count (10k) against memory exhaustion. Residual: web proxy (apps/web/src/app/api/v1/[[...path]]/route.ts) forwards client-supplied X-Forwarded-For verbatim and never sets its own, so in the documented loopback-proxy topology the per-address throttle key is attacker-controlled (spoofable/bypassable, and can be used to frame/lock out a victim IP). Implementer's own code comment already discloses this; treated as residual risk, not a criterion fail, since the per-account limit (the primary control) does not depend on address.
